## Oak Data Exploration

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

Oak Exploratory Data Analysis and Cleaning

```{r}
install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)

library(readxl)
Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean <- read_excel("Oak Project/Data/Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7&6Clean.xlsx", 
    sheet = "Input1", skip = 1)
View(Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean)
names(Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean)
```

```{r}
Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean <-
  Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean %>% #assigned by use of <- but also needed to CALL it in order for R to understand where to rename. 
  rename( Page_Num ="Page #", 
          Date = "MM/DD/YYYY",
          Recorder ="Name",
         Block ="#...4",
         Tag_Num ="#...5",
         Oak_Type ="NR, S, or A",
         Treatment ="AC, OA, NP, DT, or DL",
         OA_microclimate ="TH, TI, CN",
         Seedling_Ht_Cm ="(cm)",
         Num_Leaves ="#...10",
         Num_Dead_Leaves ="#...11",
         Leaf_Greenness ="%",
         Num_Germinated ="#...13",
         RCD ="(mm)",
        Notes  ="as written on data sheet")
Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
